svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.20.10.1 Lateral Support Required
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.20 MASONRY AND INSULATING CONCRETE FORM WALLS NOT IN CONTACT WITH THE GROUND
Lateral Support Required

g.text: Cavity wall: the thickness used for
Sentence (2) is the greater of 2/3 of the
sum of the wythe thicknesses or the
Exterior wall: supports not more than

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Masonry walls are laterally supported by floor
or roof construction or by intersecting
masonry walls or buttresses.
The spacing of these supports is not more than
(a) 20 times the wall thickness for all
loadbearing walls and exterior non-loadbearing
walls, and (b) 36 times the wall thickness for
interior non-loadbearing walls.
For Sentence (2), the thickness of a cavity
wall is taken as the greater of
(a) two-thirds of the sum of the thicknesses of
the wythes, or (b) the thickness of the thicker
wythe.
Floor and roof constructions providing this
lateral support transfer lateral loads to
walls or buttresses approximately at right
angles to the laterally supported walls.
Drawn: block walls, units without cores, floors and roofs not shown. The Article does not say where spacing is measured: shown between support faces.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.20.10.1. (page 9-147)
